source.title: Aversive prediction error signals in the amygdala

confidence_rationale: Mouse BLA hemodynamic and theta responses follow a signed temporal-difference aversive PE: shock responses shrink as the cue comes to predict shock, cue responses grow, unexpected shock evokes more than expected shock, omission drops below baseline, and the shock response predicts next-day behaviour. Supports the existence of the aversive PE TRIGGER both claims assume and the transfer of prediction from US to CS (MECH-599). It is the Rescorla-Wagner/TD half, not associability.
failure_signatures: The amygdala signal is SIGNED (omission goes below baseline), so it is a TD error, not an unsigned |PE| associability signal; it cannot by itself be the MECH-598 associability drive.
Response migrates from the shock to the predictive cue over conditioning; a threat predictor that does not show this transfer is not learning a cue-specific prediction.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In mice, BLA hemodynamic and theta responses to footshock decrease over fear conditioning while responses to the predictive tone increase; unexpected footshock evokes larger responses than expected footshock, the size of the shock response predicts next-day behaviour, and omission of an expected shock drops the response below baseline, consistent with temporal-difference models of aversive learning.
mapping.ree_translation: For MECH-598: confirms that an aversive PE event exists as a distinct signal (the trigger), and that it is signed. For MECH-599: the transfer of response from US to CS is the signature of a cue-specific conditioned threat prediction forming. It also bears on the V3-EXQ-1109 injury/threat point -- the prediction signal is not a readout of accumulated damage.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Hemodynamic and LFP signals, not single units; the TD fit is qualitative. BLA rather than CeA. Mouse. It supplies the delta-rule half that REE's harm regression already approximates, not the new associability half.
mapping.source_context: Mouse, in vivo amperometric tissue-oxygen and theta LFP in BLA during auditory fear conditioning

confidence_components.notes: Solid J Neurosci study; indirect signals. Split mapping: moderate for MECH-599 (prediction transfer), lower for MECH-598 (trigger only).
